# Provenance: feeds

Both feeds are synthetic. No printer was available, so nothing here was captured from hardware (GCP-53's "recorded" is met by checked-in message sequences in the printers' real shapes, not by a capture). Replace them with captures when a Klipper or Bambu printer is at hand.

| File | Shape | Content |
| ---- | ----- | ------- |
| `moonraker-file-position.json` | Moonraker `notify_status_update` JSON-RPC notifications carrying `virtual_sdcard.file_position` (bytes), `progress` and `is_active` (klipper@ee2c6fb:docs/Status_Reference.md:626-630) | `file_position` is the offset of a line start in `../prusaslicer/mini_cube_ps2.8.1.gcode` (85818 bytes), as Klipper reports it between lines; ascending, with repeats (Moonraker pushes unchanged values) and a last message at the final line. |
| `bambu-layer-percent.json` | Bambu MQTT `device/<serial>/report` `print` object, `push_status` with `layer_num`, `total_layer_num` and `mc_percent` | Layers 0..100 and percent 0..100 of the 100-layer `../bambu-studio/cube.gcode`. Bambu reports no byte offset, only layer and percent (D20). |

Generated by a throwaway script from the G-code file's line starts; licence of the data follows the G-code files (AGPL-3.0).

`expectedMoves` in each feed is the move `resolvePosition` gives for the message of the same index on the fixture file. The integration test waits for the marker to reach it, so the oracle never comes from the session under test; `test/feeds.test.ts` re-derives the table and fails when it drifts.
